image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (marine mollusk) adhering to a rough, light-colored rocky substrate. The chiton has an oval shape with a distinct dorsal shell composed of eight overlapping plates surrounded by a textured, leathery girdle. There is visible pinkish text/watermark in the bottom right corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior end of the organism is visible and lacks any protruding sensory structures like eyes or tentacles, consistent with chiton anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior end is blunt and indistinct.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the animal blends smoothly into the girdle without sharp definition, matching the 'blunt' description.
Surface inspection reveals no antennae, eyestalks, or other sensory appendages.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Eight distinct transverse segments (valves) are clearly visible running from head to tail, overlapping slightly.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A wide, textured band surrounds the central plates, appearing leathery and granular, consistent with a chiton girdle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plate coloration ranges from grey, brown, green to mottled patterns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plates exhibit a mottled brownish-grey coloration with subtle textural variations.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a dorsal view; the ventral foot is completely occluded by the body and substrate contact.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Can curl into defensive ball when dislodged.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a behavioral capability, not a static visual feature observable in a single image of an attached specimen.
